subject: FinOps mini-audit: prompt-path costing and final MAP gate
messages:
From: Maya Patel <maya@novuscare.com>
To: Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwood.com>, Laura Bennett <laura_bennett@redwood.com>
Date: Tue, 24 Nov 2026 09:12:00 -0800
Subject: FinOps mini-audit: prompt-path costing and final MAP gate

Marissa / Laura —

Thanks for the walkthrough yesterday. As we get towards the final mutual action plan (MAP) sign-off, finance has asked for a short, focused audit on the prompt-path unit economics so we can close procurement. The ask is narrow: confirm the tokens-per-dollar assumptions for our primary user flows and call out caching / batching expectations that could materially change the monthly run rate.

What would be most helpful from Redwood:
- A one-page table with tokens/$ by API mode for our pilot (chat vs streaming vs embeddings).
- A short note on expected prefix/KV cache hit rates for NovusCare's workload and the sweet spot for batching window (ms) vs SLA impact.
- Any non-obvious prefetch / warmup costs we should include in the 90-day forecast.

I've attached the baseline traffic sample our FinOps team exported (novuscare_promptpath_baseline.csv). Can you confirm whether the MAP acceptance criteria can be met without a dedicated reserved capacity commit? Procurement is sensitive to open spikes.

Ideally we get a short deliverable by Friday so the legal/finance teams can start approvals.

—Maya
Maya Patel
CTO, NovusCare
Attachments: novuscare_promptpath_baseline.csv (csv, 120KB)
From: Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwood.com>
To: Maya Patel <maya@novuscare.com>
Cc: Karthik Iyer <karthik_iyer@redwood.com>, Laura Bennett <laura_bennett@redwood.com>
Date: Tue, 24 Nov 2026 11:45:00 -0800
Subject: Re: FinOps mini-audit: prompt-path costing and final MAP gate

Maya —

Thanks for the sample and the clear asks. Attaching a short checklist (redwood_mini_audit_checklist.pdf) with the edits we'll run against your CSV and a first-pass tokens/$ table. High-level answers:

- Tokens/$ (first-pass, pilot mix):
  * Chat (short-turn): ~0.0033 USD/token equivalent (70% system+user+response mix)
  * Streaming (low-latency chat): ~0.0041 USD/token-equivalent due to keep-alive overhead
  * Embeddings (per vector): ~0.0009 USD/vector (64-dim baseline)

- Cache assumptions: we used a conservative 35% KV/prefix cache hit rate for your baseline. If we see 55%+ hits (higher reuse), cost is ~18-22% lower.

- Batching: default continuous-batching with a 20ms coalesce window gave the best cost/latency compromise on the sample. Increasing to 50ms improves token efficiency another ~8% but adds ~30ms median p99 tail.

- Prefetch/warmup: there is a measurable warm-up cost for cold model loads on spikes — we recommend a small reserved buffer (burst capacity) or a light pre-warm policy for high-traffic endpoints during business hours. Without reserved, short spikes will incur transient additional tokens (and sometimes cold-start latency).

Open questions we need from you to finalize by Friday:
1) Confirm target p50/p95 latency SLOs for the pilot routes (so we can map batching window trade-offs).
2) Any regulatory constraints requiring on-prem/private that would change caching (e.g., unable to cache user prompts).
3) Whether you want REDWOOD to model a 30% higher traffic spike for the first 30 days (many customers budget conservatively for launch).

If you confirm (1) and (3) today we can run a quick sim and send a one-page acceptance table + short notes for procurement/legal.

—Marissa
Marissa Cole
Senior Director, GTM Engineering
Redwood Inference
Attachments: redwood_mini_audit_checklist.pdf (1 page)
From: Karthik Iyer <karthik_iyer@redwood.com>
To: Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwood.com>, Laura Bennett <laura_bennett@redwood.com>
Cc: Maya Patel <maya@novuscare.com>
Date: Wed, 25 Nov 2026 10:05:00 -0800
Subject: Re: FinOps mini-audit: prompt-path costing and final MAP gate

Folks —

Adding a few technical clarifications based on the baseline CSV and Marissa's first-pass numbers (quoting Maya's sample):

1) Cache hit-rate sensitivity: the 35% figure is reasonable for an upper funnel with high variability. If NovusCare's flows have strong template reuse (acknowledged phrases, identical prompts), we should model 50-60% hit rates. I'll attach a short sim but to call out delta: +20ppt hit rate ≈ ~15-22% unit-cost improvement depending on request size.

2) Batching window guidance: the sample shows median inter-arrival ~18ms for the critical route; a 15–25ms coalesce seems lowest-risk. If their p95 SLA is 150ms, we can push batching to 40–50ms and still be under SLO but we must warn on p99 tail.

3) Prefetch semantics: for multi-turn flows where we can predict the next call, prefetching KV cache warms extremely cheaply compared to outright reserved GPUs. Prefetch cost shows as token-equivalent usage in our sim but is generally <5% of steady-state cost. For the first 7 days launch spike we should model a 1.1x multiplier for prefetch overhead.

4) Accounting for streaming overhead: streaming keeps a session alive and adds control tokens. In our experience factor ~1.12x additional token count vs non-streaming for comparable exchanges. If NovusCare's conversational UX uses streaming for typing feel, budget accordingly.

Attached: prefetch_sim_report.zip (small sim, CSV outputs) — I'll run a quick re-sim when Marissa confirms SLO numbers.

—Karthik
Karthik Iyer
Principal Infra Engineer, Runtime Optimization
Redwood Inference
Attachments: prefetch_sim_report.zip (sim artifact)
From: Maya Patel <maya@novuscare.com>
To: Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwood.com>
Cc: Karthik Iyer <karthik_iyer@redwood.com>, Laura Bennett <laura_bennett@redwood.com>, Finance Ops <finance@novuscare.com>
Date: Sun, 29 Nov 2026 15:03:00 -0800
Subject: Re: FinOps mini-audit: prompt-path costing and final MAP gate

Thanks — this is exactly the level of detail we needed. Confirming the SLOs: p50 45ms, p95 120ms, p99 220ms for the pilot routes. Finance is comfortable with Redwood's recommendation to model a 30% launch spike and to include a 7-day prefetch overhead at 1.1x.

Next steps for MAP close:
- Marissa: please produce the one-page tokens/$ table reflecting the confirmed SLOs and the 30% spike simulation.
- Karthik: please re-run the prefetch sim with the new SLOs and include a short sensitivity section (cache hit 30%/45%/60%).
- Legal/Finance: we will start an internal rapid review once the one-pager is in hand; expecting sign-off next week if the numbers land within the ranges discussed.

Once we have the one-pager, I'll route the MAP summary for signature. Can Redwood include a single DocuSign envelope for the MAP + SOW? If so please send the link (we prefer DocuSign).

Appreciate the quick turnaround.

—Maya
Maya Patel
CTO, NovusCare
